Keyboard shortcuts in templates, handler arguments, `<canvas>`, and many
layout fixes. Builds with Xcode 16's libc++, Bazel 8 and MSVC 17.9.

### New

- `onkey:<key>="Handler"` runs a handler when a key is pressed:
  `onkey:j="Down"`, `onkey:ArrowDown="Down"`, `onkey:ctrl+d="Jump(10)"`.
  `onkey="Typed"` runs for every key. See
  [Keyboard Shortcuts](https://arthursonzogni.github.io/RTXUI/guide/bindings#_4-keyboard-shortcuts).
- Handlers take typed arguments: `onclick="Resize(80, 24)"` calls
  `Resize(int, int)`. Integers, floats, `bool`, strings, enums (with C++26
  reflection) and any type with a `Parse()` function. Text that does not
  convert is reported.
- `<canvas ondraw="Draw" onpointer="Pointer">`: cells the application
  draws, in characters, braille dots, quadrants or half blocks, and the
  mouse in the canvas's coordinates.
- `ElementHandle::ScrollIntoView()` keeps an element in view, as the DOM's
  `scrollIntoView({block: "nearest"})`.
- `HeadlessScreen::WaitUntil()` waits for work an application does on
  another thread.
- Ctrl-Space reaches the application (`Event::CtrlSpace()`).

### Changes in behaviour

- A flex row's items keep their longest word whole
  (`overflow-wrap: break-word` is the default); `min-width: 0` or
  `overflow-wrap: anywhere` give the old behaviour.
- A flex column's items keep their content's height, as in CSS: the item
  that scrolls is the one that shrinks.
- Each key or click of a burst sees what the ones before it did.
- `onchange` on `<input>` runs when the value is committed (Enter, or the
  focus leaving), as documented.

### Fixes

- CSS no longer uses the floating-point `std::from_chars`, which Xcode 16's
  libc++ lacks: RTXUI builds on macOS 15.
- MSVC: applications fetching RTXUI get `/utf-8`, so their templates'
  non-ASCII characters are no longer garbled; builds with Visual Studio
  2022 17.9.
- Bazel: the package loads under Bazel 8.
- Layout: margins collapse between blocks, auto margins in flex and grid,
  `align-items: baseline`, `visibility`, absolute boxes, scrollbars no
  longer hide the last row, `<dialog>` sized to its content.
- Selectors: pseudo-classes in every compound (`.card:hover .title`),
  backtracking combinators, unknown pseudo-classes reported.
- The wheel scrolls an open `<select>` list; `<progress>` and `<input>`
  keep their spaces; faded borders under `opacity`.
- Hover moves are merged, and pointer moves no longer search the whole
  page for scrollbars.

### Packages

| File | What it holds |
| :--- | :--- |
| `rtxui-0.1.5-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Debug and Release static libraries, headers, CMake package, pkg-config file |
| `rtxui-0.1.5-linux-arm64.tar.gz` | The same, for arm64 |
| `rtxui-0.1.5-macos-universal.tar.gz` | The same, for arm64 and x86_64 |
| `rtxui-0.1.5-windows-x64.zip` | The same, built with MSVC (`/MD` runtime; `rtxuid.lib` for Debug) |
| `rtxui-0.1.5-windows-arm64.zip` | The same, for arm64 |
| `rtxui-0.1.5-windows-x64-mingw.zip` | The same, built with MinGW-w64 GCC, UCRT, as MSYS2's UCRT64 |
| `librtxui-dev_0.1.5_amd64.deb`, `librtxui-dev_0.1.5_arm64.deb` | Release library for Debian and Ubuntu |
| `rtxui-devel-0.1.5-1.x86_64.rpm`, `rtxui-devel-0.1.5-1.aarch64.rpm` | Release library for Fedora and other RPM distributions |
| `rtxui-0.1.5.tar.gz` | The source, as committed |

Before publishing, the release installs each .deb on Ubuntu 24.04 and each
.rpm on Fedora, and builds an app against each archive with
`find_package(rtxui)`, in Debug and in Release.

A prebuilt static C++ library links with a compatible compiler and standard
library: GCC or Clang with libstdc++ on Linux, Apple Clang on macOS, MSVC or
MinGW (UCRT) on Windows, each with its own archive. Otherwise, build from
source with FetchContent, as described in
[Getting started](https://arthursonzogni.github.io/RTXUI/guide/getting-started).
